title: QDA Finds Quantum Systems Need Data Center Integration To Become Useful
key_facts: The second international Quantum Datacenter Alliance (QDA) Forum was held at Battersea Power Station in London, with leaders from Nvidia, IBM and Equinix among those present.
The forum highlighted that system-level design, control, error correction, interoperability and power use are now seen as just as critical as the qubits themselves.
Equinix reported that hybrid infrastructure is already enabling commercial uses of quantum computing, with companies using it for high-precision molecule modelling and financial trading optimisation.
Nu Quantum's founder and CEO Carmen Palacios-Berraquero said collaboration is critical as quantum moves toward large-scale utility.
Atom Computing's CEO Ben Bloom said a utility-scale quantum computer needs many components and many collaborators, not one company.
Dame Wendy Hall said explaining quantum computing to non-technical audiences needs careful messaging to head off public concerns.
A UK science and technology department director, Hannah Boardman, said initiatives like the QDA show the value of cross-discipline collaboration.
quote_evidence: Equinix reports that hybrid infrastructure is already enabling commercial applications of quantum computing, with companies currently using the technology for high-precision molecular modelling and financial trading optimization.
Attendees emphasized that achieving fault-tolerant quantum computing requires equal attention to system-level concerns as to qubit development.
why_it_matters_hint: Industry leaders say quantum machines now need to be designed to fit inside data centers, not just built as better qubits.
event_date: QDA Forum, London; the article says the work ran over 'the past two days' (dates not given), published 2 Oct 2026.
notes: Industry group's own summary of its event, one outlet; Equinix's commercial-use claim has no figures. Same forum as C15-04.
